title: acp/1 message envelope
description: Describes the JSON that agent-comms/src/acp/models.py:Envelope actually produces via Envelope.dump() / model_dump(by_alias=True), and accepts on the way in. This is NOT a verbatim transcription of the illustrative envelope in docs/agent-communication-protocol.md ('Core model and envelope'); several fields differ from that example. See docs/decisions.md (2026-09-29, 'M1.1 schema/implementation reconciliation') for the full list, summarized per-field below.
$comment: The doc's example envelope also has a `body_format` field (e.g. "markdown"); Envelope has no such field, and pydantic silently drops unknown constructor kwargs by default, so passing body_format today has no effect and it never appears in the serialized output. `additionalProperties: false` here reflects the real, closed field set of Envelope.dump().

protocol.description: Always "acp/1" today. The protocol doc's own example envelope uses "bayto-acp/1"; the two have never matched.

message_id.description: Defaults to a bare uuid4 hex (e.g. "a357ac33..."), not the doc's "msg-<conversation>-<seq>-<rand>" shape (that shape is what the separate, non-acp/1 handoff_compat.py legacy shim produces instead).

to.description: Always a non-empty array in this implementation. The doc says a bare string is 'also accepted' as shorthand for a single recipient; Envelope's `to: list[str]` field actually rejects a bare string with a pydantic ValidationError, so that promise is not (yet) kept by the acp/1 model.

visibility.description: Free text in this implementation (only "room" is ever produced; Conversation.transcript() checks for exactly that value, and "private" is mentioned only in a code comment). The doc instead defines a closed enum: all | recipients | moderator. The two vocabularies do not overlap.

kind.description: Constrained by Envelope's `_kind_ok` field validator (code, not the JSON type system): one of acp.models.Kind's values, or any string starting with "x-" (a namespaced extension, per the doc's 'Message kinds' section). The Kind enum's values match the doc's core kind list exactly.

refs.description: An array of strings in this implementation, always empty in practice (nothing in agent-comms/src/acp ever populates it). The doc's example shows `refs` as an object map (e.g. {"output_ref": "git:9f2c1e0", "topic_version": "3"}); the legacy handoff_compat.py shim (a different, non-acp/1 format) also uses an object map for its own `refs`. Three different shapes for the same field name across this repo; see docs/decisions.md.

meta.description: Open map, as the doc specifies.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp in seconds (time.time()), not the doc's ISO-8601 string (e.g. "2026-09-28T14:02:11Z").
